comparator.name: Frisian Language and Culture
comparator.sourceNotes: The Frisian Language and Culture track is part of Groningen’s Dutch Languages and Cultures bachelor. This plan follows the September 2026 entry cohort. It combines Frisian studies, shared linguistics and literature, and a third-year minor, thesis and internship.
components: Introduction to Frisian Studies / Ynlieding Frisistyk

Choose a 10 EC course from the faculty-wide offer.
Standard Language and Language Use / Standerttaal & taalgebrûk
Shared study of Dutch and Frisian medieval literature.
Shared course in language acquisition and research methodology.
Track-specific study of Frisian language, culture and society.
Track-specific Frisian literary and language-culture study.
Research ateliers must cover both literature and linguistics for the Frisian track.
Standard Language and Language Variation / Standerttaal & Taalfariaasje
Choose a 30 EC minor from the approved offer.
Choose a 10 EC course from the faculty-wide offer.
Bachelor's Thesis — Frisian Language and Culture
The thesis follows Research Approaches and the credit requirements in the regulations. It is normally written in the language of the track.
Apply what you have learned in a Frisian language or cultural setting.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target explicitly names the Frisian Language and Culture route. The 2026-2027 TER recognizes this as the FTC track within BA Nederlandse Talen en Culturen and defines its separate course pathway, language outcomes, thesis language and field-specific second- and third-year requirements. The exact route is therefore selected independently of UCR fit.

alternatives.label: Language, communication & society
alternatives.concept: Start with everyday Dutch, stylistics and the study of how people learn and process language. Then use communication, media and sociology to explore how language and cultural identities take shape in public life.
alternatives.labelReason: Beginner Dutch, psycholinguistics, stylistics and rhetoric are the language spine. Sociology, media and politics supply social contexts.
progression: Brain and behaviour precedes Psycholinguistics. Introductory sociology precedes qualitative research and social theory, and rhetorical analysis supports later persuasive and community communication.

alternatives.label: Literature, media & cultural identity
alternatives.concept: Study how stories and images convey identity and memory. Build from literary criticism and Renaissance visual culture to memoir, adaptation, documentary and art-historical interpretation.
alternatives.labelReason: Close reading, literary theory, film and visual culture provide the central progression.
alternatives.distinctness: The literature option differs from the language option by 52.5 EC each way. It emphasises literary history, adaptation, and visual interpretation.
progression: Introductory literary criticism, stylistics and visual culture prepare for advanced interpretation, adaptation, documentary and art history.

alternatives.label: Public culture, heritage & political institutions
alternatives.concept: Explore how institutions and communities preserve, interpret and debate cultural heritage. Use comparative politics and policy analysis alongside courses on museums, collecting, public memory and historical research.
alternatives.labelReason: The option combines public institutions, policy and political participation with the study of collections, curatorial practice and heritage.
progression: Modern History, comparative politics and art history support later policy analysis, historical research, museum study and heritage debates.
alternatives.distinctness: The heritage option differs from the language option by 82.5 EC and the literature option by 82.5 EC each way. Politics, policy, museums and historical research are the main differences.

How do literature, media and heritage carry cultural identity and memory?
How do regional history, institutions and politics shape minority language and culture?

candidates.label: Frisian proficiency and field-specific Frisian studies
candidates.assessment: UCR offers one introductory Dutch course but no Frisian course, cumulative Frisian proficiency sequence, Old Frisian, Frisian linguistics, Frisian literary history, field internship or thesis in Frisian. General psycholinguistics, stylistics, literature and regional politics cannot be presented as Frisian studies.

selection.assessment: Three options develop distinct parts of the evidence: language and public communication, cultural interpretation, and heritage and political institutions. These related fields do not supply Frisian proficiency or the specialised regional curriculum. A fourth, Frisian-specific option fails on academic content.
